parameter.name: persistenceService
parameter.label: Persistence Service
parameter.description: Which persistence service holds the prediction series. Empty uses the default one. It has to be a service that can change what it already stored: influxdb, inmemory, jdbc or mongodb. A service that cannot is refused rather than used, because a prediction series that can only be appended to is not the one the system needs.

parameter.name: series
parameter.label: Prediction Series
parameter.description: Which Item carries which kind of prediction, written as role=item, for example solar-production=PV_Forecast. Each one becomes a forecast source, so a stored baseline is used whenever no live service has anything better.

parameter.name: capSeries
parameter.label: Constraint Series
parameter.description: Which Item holds the caps of which prediction Item, written as prediction=cap, for example PV_Forecast=PV_Forecast_Cap. Only used when caps are kept out of the prediction.

parameter.name: writePolicy
parameter.label: Write Policy
parameter.description: What happens when a forecast refresh lands on an entry a cap was written onto. The requirement says a refresh replaces what was there and the cap scenario says those entries hold the capped value; nothing in the specification says which wins, so owner decision D32 settled it. Caps are kept as a series of their own and applied when the prediction is read, which leaves the refreshed forecast intact underneath and is the only one of the four that survives a restart.

options.option: Newest write wins, and say so
Put the cap back after every refresh
Keep caps in their own series and apply them when reading

parameter.name: layerPrecedence
parameter.label: Layer Order
parameter.description: Which writer outranks which, written as layer=rank with the higher rank winning, for example cap=20. Layers are baseline, forecast, cap and learned. Only used by the layer-order write policy, which refuses to write at all until this is declared.

parameter.name: demandItem
parameter.label: Demand Item
parameter.description: The Item the derived heating-demand series is published to. Empty publishes nothing: the derived series is still readable by the energy engine, it simply is not written anywhere.

parameter.name: heatLoss
parameter.label: Heat Loss
parameter.description: How much heating power the building needs per degree of difference to the outside, in kilowatts per kelvin. There is no default, because this is a property of the building. Until it is declared, no heating demand is derived at all and the system reports that rather than deriving a number nobody chose.

parameter.name: baseTemperature
parameter.label: Base Temperature
parameter.description: The outdoor temperature below which the building needs heating.

parameter.name: solarGain
parameter.label: Solar Gain
parameter.description: How much heating need one kilowatt-hour of the solar forecast displaces. It stands for the glazing and the orientation together, which is why it is useful on a site with no solar panels at all. Undeclared means a solar forecast changes nothing.

parameter.name: preheatHorizon
parameter.label: Pre-heating Horizon
parameter.description: How far ahead to look for a temperature drop worth pre-heating for.

parameter.name: preheatDrop
parameter.label: Pre-heating Drop
parameter.description: How much colder the coming hours have to be before demand is pulled forward.

parameter.name: preheatShare
parameter.label: Pre-heating Share
parameter.description: How much of the coming extra need is pulled into the warmer hours, between 0 and 1.

parameter.name: preheatModel
parameter.label: Pre-heating Bookkeeping
parameter.description: Whether the energy pulled forward is added to the day or taken out of the hours it was pre-heating for. The specification asks for the rise and does not say which, so there is no default and pre-heating stays off until all four of these are declared.
